what_its_for: Griseofulvin is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, hair, and nails. This includes ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch, and fungal nail infections. It works by stopping the fungus from growing so your body can clear the infection.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Take it WITH food, especially a fatty meal like peanut butter or whole milk, because this helps your body absorb the medicine better. Swallow the tablet whole or you may crush and mix it with food or liquid if swallowing is difficult. Take it at the same time every day to keep it working. Do NOT skip doses even if you feel better — finish the full course of treatment.
dosing: Your dose depends on your weight, age, and the type of infection being treated. Adults usually take 500 mg to 1,000 mg per day, either as a single dose or split into smaller doses. Children's doses are based on body weight. Your doctor will tell you the right dose for you. Treatment may last from 2 to 4 weeks for skin infections, up to 4 to 6 months for nail infections, so be patient and keep taking it.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused medicine properly — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol can cause flushing, fast heartbeat, nausea, and make you feel very unwell. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or trouble concentrating. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds because this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight — use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid taking antacids or other medicines that could interact without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a severe skin rash, hives, or peeling skin; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools; severe stomach pain; unusual bruising or bleeding; confusion or numbness and tingling in hands or feet; or if your infection gets worse or does not improve after several weeks of treatment. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within the first few weeks, but it is very important to keep taking the medicine for the full prescribed period even if symptoms improve. Skin infections may clear up in 2 to 4 weeks. Scalp or hair infections may take 4 to 6 weeks. Nail infections can take several months to fully heal because nails grow slowly. Stopping too soon can allow the fungus to come back.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or trying to become pregnant. Women should use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least one month after stopping. Men should use condoms during treatment and for 6 months after stopping. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: This medicine can be used in children and the dose is based on their weight — your doctor will calculate the right amount. Elderly patients: Use with caution; your doctor may monitor you more closely for side effects. Liver disease: This medicine may not be safe if you have serious liver problems — tell your doctor about any liver conditions before starting.
